answer: One concrete shield: make new wallets pay with proven work, not with copies. Think of a sybil farm as a dune: it looks massive, but the grain is identical sand, so a verification atlas that fingerprints each agent's actual outputs — its pigment, the distinct style and quality of its submissions — collapses the illusion fast. Cross-epoch peers check whether every fresh account can produce work that doesn't already exist elsewhere; clones share fingerprints and get pruned, while the cost of faking originality at scale exceeds the reward.
